memo.verdict: PARK, medium-high conviction. Composite grade C. Direction neutral on the business, tilted bearish on the equity at EUR 74.4. The memo declines progression to Early-Stage Assessment on valuation and case-simplicity grounds, explicitly not on business-quality grounds, and keeps FQT-AT on the active watchlist with no research budget allocated until a progression criterion trips. The memo ADOPTS the risks report's own stage recommendation in full: that report recommends "deferring the core investment allocation until cash conversion catches up with rapid revenue growth" and its final progression verdict is that "the high probability of a False Friend profile warrants a neutral hold-and-watch stance". There is therefore no divergence between memo and risks report to reconcile. Progression requires any two of six named reassessment criteria, with the FY26 preliminary print on 17 February 2027 as the first observation date.
case: The memo's argument runs in four moves, in this order.

First, the change forces are real, external and largely statutory. Element E1 required attribute 1 grades B, above the peer-set median, because the demand is legally compelled rather than budget-discretionary. European defence equipment spending rose 39% in 2024 and was expected to exceed EUR 100bn in 2025, on the EUR 800bn ReArm Europe framework. The European ATM Master Plan and SESAR oblige air navigation providers to move to virtualised architectures, and Deutsche Flugsicherung took Europe's first cloud-native deployment at the Munich backup centre. NIS-2 and the Critical Entities Resilience Directive carry fines up to EUR 10m or 2% of global revenue, forcing replacement of non-compliant legacy control systems. Emergency services and railways must migrate off legacy TETRA and GSM-R to 5G mission-critical services and rail communications standards. Frequentis completed 15,000 air-to-ground protocol converters for the US Department of Transportation's USD 12.5bn programme, compressing an eight-year schedule into twelve months. The forces are converting into contracts: order intake rose 16.5% in FY25 and 17.0% in H1 2026. Internal change is orderly but incremental and grades only C: a chief technology officer appointed on 1 July 2024 specifically to drive the software-centric cloud migration, the Nemergent stake taken from 24.83% to 51% in July 2026 securing a sovereign European 5G mission-critical stack, and the Tait Communications agreement as the first pure software-licence channel.

Second, the business quality behind those forces is genuinely high, which is why Element E11 grades B and Group 3 grades B. The moat is mechanical, not reputational: full ICAO compliance plus NATO quality assurance certification creates a near-insurmountable barrier for new software entrants, replacing an active control room risks national-infrastructure downtime and expensive controller retraining, and systems remain operational for decades so the replacement window opens rarely. Element E11 required attribute 2 core question 3, on vanilla new entrants, grades A on that basis. The regulator is the strongest actor in the value chain and it is on the company's side: Element E11 required attribute 4 core question 1 grades A, with a Frequentis director elected president of the European aviation standardisation body in April 2026. Demand is durable, with over 90% public-authority revenue, zero material historical defaults, and an installed base at 54% of FY25 sales. Frequentis leads rather than suffers the disruptions, with digital towers at 12 customers across 16 airports delivering up to 80% capital-expenditure savings, nationwide civil drone platforms in Sweden and Lithuania, military uncrewed traffic management tested across 1,400 flights for the German armed forces, and the first fully public-cloud emergency control room in the United Kingdom.
counter_case: The risks report's own recommendation, quoted in the memo and adopted rather than argued against: defer the core investment allocation until cash conversion catches up with rapid revenue growth, on a neutral hold-and-watch stance, because the competing-hypotheses matrix names the FALSE FRIEND profile the winner with zero hard inconsistencies. In that profile, a record order backlog masks working-capital pre-financing strain and early-stage margin dilution, upfront project start-up costs dilute margins because long-term contracts yield lower contribution margins in their first years, and the transition requires massive cash outlays for pre-financing.
The strongest counter to the memo's own park verdict, carried at four separate points:
triggers: Six reassessment criteria. Re-open Triaging only when at least two are met; a single criterion is noise, though the price test alone would justify a fresh look.
1. Phasing test. FY26 EBIT margin delivered at or above 7.0% with H2 2026 order intake above EUR 300m, observable at the February 2027 preliminary trading update.
2. Margin test. Air Traffic Management segment EBIT margin above 6.5% for a full year, from 4.9% in FY25, evidencing the software convergence actually landing.
3. Mix test. Gross margin recovering to 72% or better, from 68.0% in H1 2026, evidencing that growth is no longer being bought with hardware.
4. Price test. The forward multiple de-rating below 20x, or the published fair value moving decisively above the share price.
5. Coverage test. A second broker initiating coverage, breaking the single-broker monopoly and giving revision data genuine informational content.
